doc.name: A — meal kit catalogue, monochrome colour block, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: recipe box with produce
Category: meal kit
Shot programme: monochrome colour block
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are a commercial stills director briefing a meal kit capture. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the shadow-play silhouette in a monochrome colour block treatment.

SUBJECT. A recipe box with produce. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Backlit so the product edge glows and the set falls into shadow. Shoot on an 8mm circular fisheye at f/4, framing for frame-within-frame using foreground architecture.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a ring light on axis for flat, modern, shadowless coverage. Stage the product on or against wet river stone, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward high-contrast teal-and-orange with protected mid-tone skin. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a book light bounce producing an extremely soft wrap. Stage the product on or against mirrored steel, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a sun-bleached grade with faded blacks and a green-yellow bias. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.
